question: There are strong indications of dominant position and anti-competitive practices in the payment services space. This is of great concern for millions of small European merchants who rely on these services to make ends meet. The pricing of these services does not seem fair and it is not transparent.

In 2019, the Commission adopted decisions against Visa1 and Mastercard2 on grounds of unjustified pricing connected to interchange fees. In response, Visa and Mastercard offered legally binding commitments to reduce interchange fees. Recently, European retailers have publicly demanded antitrust action in relation to ‘scheme fees’. These fees are charged by the card networks to the acquiring banks.

Banks typically pass these costs on to merchants in the form of a merchant service charge. In response, the Commission, has opened two separate cases (AT.39398 and AT.40049). The Commission is asked: 1.
What stage of investigation are these cases currently at? When are the preliminary results expected?

If the Commission finds evidence of predatory pricing or collusion, would the new decision be treated as a separate incident or would it be seen in conjunction with previous decisions, as a violation of the legally binding commitments made by Visa and Mastercard in 2019?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.2.2026) In 2019, the Commission made legally binding commitments by Visa and MasterCard to reduce their multilateral interchange fees for payments in the European Economic Area (EEA) with consumer cards issued elsewhere (inter-regional interchange fees). These proceedings related to cases registered under number AT.39398 and AT.40049.

The commitments were set to be in place until November 2024 but were voluntarily continued by Visa and Mastercard for another five years until November 2029. Separately, the Commission is conducting an investigation in relation to an alleged lack of transparency of card scheme and processing services and corresponding fees that Visa and MasterCard charge to acquirers in the EEA.

This investigation is at a preliminary stage and is ongoing, and therefore no further information can be provided at this stage. This investigation is independent from the proceedings under case numbers AT.39398 and AT.40049 (which were closed through commitments).
